findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, which is visible via the instance metadata service and Terraform state, risking credential theft.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and recoverable if the underlying storage is compromised or the snapshot is exposed.
The snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of the source volume, so sensitive data captured in the snapshot is stored unencrypted and could be shared/copied without protection.
Ingress rule opens TCP port 22 (SSH) to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing any host on the internet to attempt administrative access to the instance.

Ingress rule opens TCP port 80 to 0.0.0.0/0; combined with map_public_ip_on_launch and an internet gateway, this exposes the web service broadly, and while HTTP is expected to be public for a web host, it also lacks any TLS termination, meaning traffic is served in cleartext.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to all instances launched in this subnet, increasing internet exposure of workloads that may not need to be public.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block/ACL restrictions defined, risking unencrypted storage and potential public exposure of network flow log data.
